attribute_reduction.other: None reached. Default §108(b)(1) order hits net operating losses first (irc_108.md (b)(1)(A)); the NOL pool (6,100,000.00) absorbs the full excluded amount (5,460,000.00), so the reduction never reaches general business credits, minimum tax credit, capital loss carryovers, basis of property, passive activity losses, or foreign tax credits. No such other attributes appear in the client file; confirm none exist (QUESTIONS.md § Session 3). Reductions are made after the tax for the year of discharge is determined (irc_108.md (b)), i.e., after the tax for the year containing the 9/30/2026 effective date (Dkt. 214). Ordering caveat: §108(b)(1)(A) per the library covers 'net operating losses and net operating loss carryovers to such year' — the NOL generated BY the discharge year (the year containing 9/30/2026) is consumed before older carryovers. The only attribute figure in the client file is the petition-date NOL of 6,100,000.00 (plan_term_sheet.md); projected 2026 taxable income/NOL is not in the file (QUESTIONS.md). nol_before/nol_after above assume no additional 2026 NOL; if 2026 itself generates an NOL, the total 5,460,000.00 reduction is unchanged but it consumes that first and preserves more of the 6,100,000.00 carryover. Arithmetic: GUC allowed claim 8,400,000.00 (plan_term_sheet.md, adopted by the confirmed plan); plan pays 35% cash = 8,400,000.00 x 0.35 = 2,940,000.00 over 24 months, first installment on the effective date (both the 35%/$2,940,000.00 and the 24-month/first-installment terms are stated in Dkt. 214); discharged = 8,400,000.00 - 2,940,000.00 = 5,460,000.00. Cross-check: the Dkt. 214 payment figure ties to the term-sheet allowed amount — 2,940,000.00 / 0.35 = 8,400,000.00. The first installment paid in cash on 9/30/2026 does not change these figures — amounts actually paid under the plan are never discharged, so only the 5,460,000.00 balance arising by reason of the effective-date discharge is COD income. Assumption: GUC is the only impaired class — DIP is repaid in full per the confirmed plan, and the other 7,800,000.00 of the 16,200,000.00 effective-date claims/post-petition liabilities (figure restated in Dkt. 214) are paid in full (composition not itemized in the client file — flagged). 'cod_income' is the gross amount arising by reason of the discharge; taxable inclusion after the §108(a)(1)(A) exclusion is 0.00. Discharge in a title 11 case is excluded in full under §108(a)(1)(A) with no insolvency limitation (irc_108.md).

election_108b5: no — no demonstrable benefit on the file's facts. Default ordering reduces the NOL by the whole 5,460,000.00 (6,100,000.00 -> 640,000.00) and leaves the 3,200,000.00 tax basis of depreciable property untouched (basis per plan_term_sheet.md). Electing §108(b)(5) (irc_108.md (b)(5)) would instead apply 3,200,000.00 against depreciable-property basis (to zero) and only 2,260,000.00 against the NOL (NOL after = 3,840,000.00). The reduction is 5,460,000.00 either way, and the future deductions LEFT in these two attributes are 3,840,000.00 either way — default: 640,000.00 NOL + 3,200,000.00 depreciable basis; election: 3,840,000.00 NOL + 0.00 basis (640,000.00 + 3,200,000.00 = 3,840,000.00 = 3,840,000.00 + 0.00) — so the election merely swaps depreciation deductions on assets the reorganized company keeps using for NOL carryforwards; fresh-start reporting does NOT apply (see fresh_start.md), so under the default the retained depreciation basis remains the company's book/tax basis in those assets. The library contains only §108; whether the NOLs carry expiration dates or usage limits is NOT in the library and cannot be verified. If tax returns show NOLs near expiration, revisit with tax counsel before filing; absent that, do not elect.
